meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (International Company regime, Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid legal system based on English common law statutes, indigenous custom (fa‘a Samoa), and statutory company law

International Companies (Amendment) Act 2014); Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 (Samoa); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2000 (Samoa); Customs Act 2014 (Samoa); International Companies (Licensed Agent) Regulations

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport for each shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the holder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Incumbency listing directors, officers, and registered shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed registered agent in Samoa or corporate services provider

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds wealth statement
Certificate of Good Standing for any corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicable companies registry of the foreign jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized specimen signature card and authorized signatory list
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate ownership chart and UBO declaration with proportionate ownership percentages
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant company and responsible compliance officer

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced CDD screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, and the licensed customs broker representative against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit watchlists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists, INTERPOL notices, and, given USD ACH/wire clearing rails, OFAC SDN and Foreign Sanctions Evaders lists. Written risk assessment and screening evidence must be retained for a minimum of five years and refreshed annually or upon any material ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa — applications filed exclusively through a licensed International Company registered agent using the MCIL Companies Office commercial registry portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be submitted in English or Gagana Samoa; any foreign-script name (including Chinese characters) must be presented in romanized transliteration, and the Latin-alphabet rendering is the controlling registered name. Chinese-character trade names may be used informally but carry no statutory registration effect.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any name identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or reserved name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: file a renewal application with MCIL through the registered agent prior to expiry and pay the renewal reservation fee. Rejection: submit a written appeal to the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the refusal notice, stating grounds and attaching a letter of no-objection from any relevant regulator (e.g., Central Bank of Samoa for banking tokens, Samoa Customs Service for 'Customs/Brokerage' tokens); where ministerial consent applies, obtain prior written approval from the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour. Simultaneously, a modified name can be re-submitted to avoid incorporation delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the licensed customs brokerage activity. The International Companies Act requires a physical registered office at the premises of a licensed registered agent in Samoa. Additionally, the Samoa Customs Service broker license mandates a physical place of business in Samoa and a resident licensed customs broker representative, making a pure virtual-office arrangement legally inadequate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-high quantified risk: approximately 30-50% probability of an unannounced physical compliance inspection by Samoa Customs Service or the Financial Intelligence Unit within the first 12 months of operation due to the medium-risk AML classification of customs brokerage.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Samoa) and foreign competent authorities

First-year annual International Company license fee

Pre-incorporation legal due diligence opinion and jurisdiction analysis (local counsel)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss. 5-13, 23-24; Companies Regulations 1988 (as amended); International Business Facilitation Act 2000, Part III
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association of an International Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for International Companies; US$1.00 nominal share capital is acceptable; no escrow account deposit or capital verification requirement applies
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED that the International Company adopts its Memorandum and Articles as filed and that the Company's liability is limited by shares. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED that the inaugural members subscribe to and allot 1,000 ordinary shares of US$1.00 each to the founding shareholder at par. The registered office shall be the address of the licensed registered agent in Samoa. [Name] is appointed sole Director, [Name] is appointed Company Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Compliance Officer for the licensed customs brokerage activity. The appointed officers are authorised to open bank accounts, instruct counsel, and execute the Customs Broker Licence application before Samoa Customs Service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability inquiry to the MCIL Companies Registry with a proposed corporate name and the term 'Limited'. Upon approval, pay the reservation fee and obtain a written name reservation certificate valid for 30 days. Ensure the name does not resemble any existing international company or contain restricted words such as 'Bank' or 'Trust' without ministerial consent.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged as deceptively similar, file a written objection with the Registrar offering a revised name; the Registrar renders a decision within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Samoan registered agent or local attorney at law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage the licensed registered agent to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, including clauses on limited liability, share capital, director powers, and the regulated customs brokerage object. Each subscriber must sign the incorporation contents page before a notary public in Samoa, and the agent must complete the Certificate of Registered Agent endorsing the instrument.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (draft, signed by subscribers)
Notarized passport copies of subscribers and intended directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry or notary queries omissions, amend the instrument by resolution of subscribers and re-sign; no additional registry fee is incurred for corrections made before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation application with registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Memorandum and Articles, together with the statutory filing form and government fee schedule, to the Companies Registry. Payment may be made by bank draft or electronic transfer into the MCIL designated government account. The application must state the registered office address in Samoa and the names of the first director and secretary.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association (3 copies)
Statutory declaration of compliance by registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect notice or extends the assessment period, submit a written explanation and corrected documents within 14 days; the Registrar may impose a late-compliance penalty of US$50 per additional working day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation dated the same day as filing. Verify that the certificate bears the company number, the exact corporate name, and the statement that the company is incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987. The registered agent shall retain the original certificate and provide certified copies.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (original issued by MCIL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error in name or date, return the certificate to the Registrar with an affidavit of correction; the Registrar issues a replacement within 3 working days without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting, registered office acknowledgment, and officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company; supervised by MCIL registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board of directors' meeting (in person or by telephone/electronic consent) at which the board passes the First Board Resolution adopting the share issuance, registered office, and officer appointments. Minutes must be signed by the chair and the secretary, and a copy lodged with the registered agent. The registered agent files the annual license fee schedule and confirms the registered office address with the Registry.
required_dossiers: Consent of director and secretary to act
Registered office acknowledgment letter from the agent
Proof of payment of annual government license fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry notes a defect in officer appointments or ownership records, file an amended notice of director/secretary change and a corrective resolution within 10 working days; late filings attract a US$100 penalty but do not invalidate third-party contracts entered before cure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa Customs Service, Ministry for Revenue, Apia
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Broker Licence under the Customs Act 1976 (as amended), Part XI; accompanying Security Bond in favour of Samoa Customs Service

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Registration level (office-based customs brokerage; no full Environmental Impact Assessment Report required)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 and the Waste Management Act 2005; office waste to be collected under Apia municipal contract; no significant industrial wastewater discharge, VOCs, or hazardous air emissions; electronic bond-management operations must maintain records of duty-free goods handling under Customs Secretary directive

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Clearance Certificate from the National Fire and Emergency Services Authority (NFESA) verifying occupancy load, extinguishers, and evacuation routes; structural load certification from the Land Transport Authority / MCIL building inspectorate; workplace health clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002 confirming ergonomic workstations, safe electrical installations, and adequate staff amenities; additionally, the principal customs broker must hold a valid employment contract and pass the Customs Service fit-and-proper check.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue – Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), online portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity must apply for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) by submitting the Corporate Registration Form (IR-C1), certified certificate of incorporation, attested constitutional documents, and proof of appointment of the local registered agent. International Companies receive a TIN upon incorporation under the International Companies Act 1987. A separate VAGST registration must be filed with the SRA when taxable supplies exceed the statutory threshold; foreign entities may appoint a locally resident fiscal representative for VAGST compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. An International Company may, through a formal application to the Ministry for Revenue, elect to be treated as a resident ordinary company (domestic company election), thereby becoming fully taxable on worldwide income and able to access tax treaty benefits. Hybrid mismatch limitation rules are not directly applicable to exempt International Companies but would apply upon conversion to resident taxable status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa has not implemented a national real-time e-invoicing clearance or digital stamping mandate as of the current date. VAGST invoices must contain prescribed particulars and be issued within the statutory timeframe. Electronic invoicing is permitted through standard B2B systems. All import and export clearance is executed electronically through the SRA's ASYCUDA World customs management system, which provides an API/Gateway interface for customs brokers; brokers must hold a valid broker license and digital machine-readable card linked to the ASYCUDA World user profile. No fiscal stamping is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Samoa in accordance with the Customs Management Act are zero-rated when the supplier holds the export documentation and the goods are exported within the statutory time period. Services, including customs brokerage and forwarding services, are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident customer and the direct benefit is outside Samoa; however, brokerage services physically performed in Samoa connected to imported goods, or services directly for the benefit of a resident importer, are standard-rated. Zero-rating for a customs brokerage house should be documented by identifying the non-resident principal, showing the direct link to the exported goods, and retaining all clearance records showing the goods exited Samoa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CED) submitted in ASYCUDA World with broker reference code
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a licensed Samoan commercial bank showing foreign exchange repatriation for the export supply
Commercial invoice and purchase order identifying the non-resident customer and the zero-rated brokerage fee
Certificate of Shipment / customs release authorization or electronic Customs Permit confirming goods left the territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or fraudulent zero-rating claims attract an automatic penalty of 150% of the tax shortfall plus interest, and civil penalties under the VAGST Act and Customs Management Act may be imposed up to WST 200,000 or three times the duty/VAGST evaded, whichever is greater. Criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment for up to seven years. Retrospective clawback applies for four years from the end of the accounting period in respect of ordinary errors; there is no time limit for fraud or deliberate misstatement. The Commissioner of the Samoa Revenue Authority is empowered to seize assets and impose maritime or border compliance penalties on the exporting principal and the broker as a licensed customs agent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, is the statutory foreign exchange and payments authority; day-to-day administration is delegated to authorised dealers (the licensed commercial banks) under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Foreign Exchange Regulations 1977. An International Company (IC) holding a valid international company certificate from the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) is exempt from the Exchange Control Act 1976 for transactions concluded in foreign currency and performed wholly outside Samoa (exemptions under the International Companies Act 2017). Any WST-denominated transaction with a Samoan resident falls back within CBS jurisdiction and destroys the exemption.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a managed, thinly traded currency and is not deliverable offshore. Current-account convertibility is available for genuine trade and service payments through authorised dealers, subject to documentary proof and CBS reporting thresholds; capital-account remittances (dividends, capital repatriation) require CBS approval unless the IC exemption applies. Profit-remittance hurdle: to preserve the exemption, the customs brokerage IC must invoice, collect and settle exclusively in USD or AUD; collecting WST from domestic importers would trigger onshore exchange control, jeopardise the IC's tax-exempt status and require a separate Samoan-licensed entity. The blueprint therefore keeps the IC treasury 100% foreign-currency and routes domestic duty flows through a licensed local intermediary.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For Samoan-resident exporters, export proceeds must be repatriated into Samoa within 6 months of shipment and, where directed by an authorised dealer under s.7 of the Exchange Control Act 1976, be offered for sale into WST promptly upon receipt. This statutory surrender rule has no application to an exempt IC, provided brokerage commissions are earned offshore and invoiced in foreign currency; each incoming remittance should carry a brokerage contract reference to evidence non-resident service provision. No WST receipts may be booked into the IC's operating account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Limited (BSP Samoa) — Apia
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD/AUD multi-currency; primary IC clearing account)
Capital Escrow Account / Trust Account for client customs duty funds
Operational Account (backup settlement and local threshold transactions)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary clearing rail; Medium only as an ancillary collections and payout channel. Offshore digital EMIs (UK FCA, EU-licensed, MAS-licensed) are not supervised by the Central Bank of Samoa and cannot engage in WST settlement; their utility is limited to holding USD/GBP/EUR float for foreign broker disbursements. Practical constraints: EMIs impose jurisdiction-based enhanced due diligence on Samoan ICs, require a reference letter from BSP or SCB, and cannot route funds to the Samoa Revenue Authority or Samoan importers. Recommended use is a USD payout wallet with a top-tier SWIFT-enabled EMI for disbursements below USD 10,000, mirrored monthly into the BSP Samoa account for CBS audit trail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoan law does not require directors to be physically present to open a corporate account, and remote opening is technically permitted where apostilled corporate documents and a CBS 'fit and proper' video interview are completed. In practice, all licensed banks require at least one in-person signatory visit to Apia to execute the account mandate and banking covenants. Recommended execution: one IC director travels to Apia for two business days for a scheduled face-to-face compliance interview; remaining offshore beneficial owners may stay remote, provided their passports, proof of address and source-of-funds statements are apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention (Samoa is a party) and dated within three months of submission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IC incorporated under 12 months with wholly non-resident directors and nominal paid-up capital — classic shell-company red flag under CBS AML/CFT guidelines and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIFA Certificate of Good Standing; licensed registered agent undertaking; full beneficial ownership schedule; certified passport copies of all directors; 12-month source-of-wealth bank statements from the home jurisdiction; introducer letter from a licensed foreign bank; minimum initial capital deposit of USD 100,000 to evidence substantive operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customs brokerage inherently involves third-party funds movement (importer duty payments passing through the broker), creating concentration and co-mingling risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customs Broker Licence issued under the Customs Management Act 2006; trust account deed and bank-approved escrow accounting policy; monthly reconciliation ledger mapping client deposits to Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) payments; AML/CFT programme containing client due diligence procedures; designated compliance officer endorsed by the registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure, adverse media, or high-risk jurisdiction indicators in the beneficial ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative sanctions screening report against UN, EU, and OFAC lists for each beneficial owner; apostilled police clearance from the country of residence of each director; sworn statutory declaration of source of funds for every capital injection above USD 50,000; bank introduction letter from the home-country relationship manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering mismatch between declared cargo value and value of funds flowing through the broker's account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-transaction file containing bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, SRA customs declaration (ASYCUDA World receipt) and carrier freight statement; bank reconciliation mapped to each declaration; quarterly independent audit certificate furnished to the bank's compliance team.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for subscribed capital: the beneficial owner remits USD by SWIFT MT103 to the IC's BSP Samoa operational account (or SCB escrow account) with the purpose description 'IC Share Capital Contribution — International Companies Act 2017'; the receiving bank performs enhanced due diligence and wires above USD 1,000,000 are held pending the share allotment resolution, updated share register and source-of-funds evidence. Verification bundle: Certificate of Incorporation, allotment board resolution, updated share register, SIFA maintenance receipt. No Samoan capital-import certificate is required. Any accidental WST credit must be immediately converted to USD or AUD to preserve the offshore-transaction exemption.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails in priority order: (1) overseas broker/agent fees and foreign customs authority payments — SWIFT MT103 direct from BSP Samoa via its correspondent network (BSP Port Moresby or ANZ/HSBC Singapore) with evidence of the underlying brokerage contract; (2) US border clearance payments — Automated Broker Interface (ABI) and ACH credits executed through the bank's USD correspondent account and reconciled against ABI release records; (3) duty payments to Samoa Revenue Authority — electronic transfer to SRA's CBS treasury account referencing the ASYCUDA World declaration number, routed exclusively through a licensed local intermediary in WST; (4) commercial letters of credit to foreign bonding houses for high-value customs bonds — sight LC issued by BSP Samoa with 30% cash margin. All transactions above USD 10,000 are subject to CBS reporting and may be suspended if supporting documentation is incomplete.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward WST/USD up to 12 months from authorised dealers, permissible only with evidence of an underlying customs brokerage contract and CBS exemption confirmation; not available on a speculative basis.

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) WST/USD executed with a licensed bank in Singapore or Hong Kong under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, cash-settled in USD; permissible because the IC's exposure is booked in USD and WST is not deliverable offshore.

Cross-currency swap (USD against AUD/GBP/EUR) with an offshore counterparty for matched funding of long-term brokerage receivable portfolios, subject to board resolution and a documented hedge-budget policy.

Plain-vanilla FX options (USD call / WST put) via offshore bank counterparties for contingent exposure in duty refund cycles, generally subject to minimum notional thresholds around USD 250,000 due to low onshore market depth.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Return and Annual License Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) / Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days following the anniversary date of incorporation; recurring annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharge of 10% on the unpaid annual fee plus WST 250 (USD 95) late-filing penalty; the Registrar may initiate strike-off proceedings after 3 months of arrears; company is administratively dissolved and its assets vest in the State after 12 months of continuous default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Customs Broker License Annual Renewal (Customs Clearance Brokerage Operation - ISIC 5229)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the license expiry date printed on the SRA Customs License (standard annual cycle validated to 31 December); renewal application accepted within the 60-day window preceding expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic license lapse at expiry; brokerage activity without a valid license constitutes an offence under the Customs Management Act 2011 carrying a criminal fine of up to WST 1,000 (USD 375) plus WST 50 (USD 19) per continuing day; ASYCUDA clearance privileges suspended until full reinstatement, and a new application requires fresh licensing review

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies / SIFA Online Registry Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 business days after the incorporation anniversary; supplemental UBO update due within 7 days after any share transfer or ownership change exceeding 10% of issued share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 100 per return; willful false confirmation is a criminal offence punishable by a fine up to WST 50,000 (USD 18,900) or up to 5 years imprisonment; directors may be held personally liable and the registered agent's filing privileges may be suspended

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business License Annual Renewal for Onshore Customs Brokerage Operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Business Registration Division / Samoa Revenue Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the business license expiry date stated on the certificate (renewal cycle of 12 consecutive months), normally aligned with the revenue period ending 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a valid business license is an offence under the Business Licences Act 1998; fine up to WST 3,000 (USD 1,130) plus daily penalty of WST 100 (USD 38); license may be revoked for repeated default and the customs brokerage premises may be ordered closed by MCIL

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is not an automatic annual duty for a Samoa International Company. A mandatory independent audit is triggered when: (i) gross assets exceed WST 2,000,000 (USD 740,000); (ii) gross annual revenue exceeds WST 1,000,000 (USD 370,000); (iii) the company has more than 25 members or 25 beneficial owners; or (iv) the Registrar of International Companies or the Samoa Revenue Authority directs an audit as a condition of customs broker license renewal.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements prepared in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Samoa; qualifying entities may apply IFRS for SMEs. Books and accounting records must be sufficient to give a true and fair view, must be maintained in English, and may be expressed in Samoa Tala or in the directors' designated currency of record approved by the registered agent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent issues a certification package at least 21 days before the incorporation anniversary; the directors must identify every ultimate natural person holding a 10% or greater beneficial interest, providing full name, date of birth, nationality, residential address, and the exact percentage of ownership; all share transfers during the preceding 12 months must be evidenced by the instrument of transfer, entered on the register of members, and disclosed on the confirmation filing; the certified confirmation is filed through the SIFA online registry within 15 business days after the anniversary; any subsequent transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership within the year must be reported to the UBO register within 7 calendar days of the event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Secretaries and Registered Agent
Minute Book (of directors' and shareholders' resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,200 (annual retained fee for a licensed Samoa registered agent and registered office services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 4,500 (incurred only if the audit thresholds are exceeded or an audit is directed by the SRA or Registrar; a standard small customs brokerage IC below thresholds typically incurs no audit fee)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% - Samoa International Company (IC) exemption under the International Companies Act 1987; standard resident-company corporate income tax headline rate is 27% under the Income Tax Act 2017
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The IC is entirely exempt from Samoa corporate income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, and non-resident withholding tax on distributions, provided it carries on no business in Samoa and derives no Samoa-source income. The only recurring cost is the annual SIFA license fee. Domestic trading companies, including a domestic customs brokerage licensee, are subject to the standard 27% CIT on net Samoa-source profits with no statutory tax holidays available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SIFA Annual Return of International Company (AR-IC); electronic lodgment through the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) e-Services portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 90 days immediately following each anniversary of the date of incorporation of the International Company

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, incorporation number, and date of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exactly as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; no abbreviations unless registered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office and registered agent in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be a licensed SIFA registered agent located in Samoa; a postal box of the company itself is not a valid registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized share capital band, director details, and shareholder register
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may be listed directly; beneficial ownership particulars must be disclosed separately to the registered agent for AML/CFT record-keeping.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of no business carried on in Samoa (domestic trading prohibition certification)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify customs brokerage and bonded transit services are performed exclusively for offshore or non-Samoan-resident clients; any on-island brokerage activity for Samoan importers converts the IC to domestic taxable status and violates the International Companies Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual license fee calculation and payment schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate the fee according to the authorized share capital band; remit via the licensed registered agent or by direct wire transfer to SIFA in WST.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late lodgment triggers a SIFA late-filing penalty of 10% of the annual license fee plus a monthly surcharge of 1% on the unpaid fee; non-filing for two consecutive years results in administrative strike-off, loss of limited-liability protection, revocation of good-standing status, and disclosure of the default to foreign tax authorities.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for Samoa International Companies on distributions of exempt profits to non-resident shareholders; 15% statutory non-resident dividend withholding tax applies to dividends paid by a resident domestic Samoan company to non-residents
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: 1) Confirm treaty eligibility and that the shareholder is a resident of a jurisdiction with an applicable Samoa DTA; 2) obtain a Certificate of Residence / Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's resident tax authority; 3) submit a treaty relief application, the TRC, and a beneficial ownership declaration to the Samoan payer or the Ministry of Revenue (Inland Revenue) prior to the distribution date; 4) the Ministry verifies the minimum shareholding holding period and beneficial ownership, then approves the reduced rate (typically 5% for shareholdings of at least 10%, and 15% for portfolio holdings); 5) if relief is not approved before payment, the full statutory rate must be withheld and a refund claim may be lodged afterwards.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: 15% final withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents and 15% final withholding tax on royalties paid to non-residents. Under standard Samoa DTA terms, interest is reduced to 10% and royalties to 10%, subject to beneficial ownership verification and limitation-on-benefits provisions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File equivalent) is mandatory where the aggregate value of related-party transactions exceeds WST 500,000 per annum; a Country-by-Country Report is required only where consolidated group revenue meets the OECD threshold and Samoa has an active competent-authority exchange arrangement in force.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable. Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations under the International Companies Act 1987 apply to relevant activities, including 'distribution and service centre' activity, which covers customs clearance brokerage and bonded transit management. A Samoa IC must maintain within Samoa: (i) direction and management of the activity, (ii) a minimum number of qualified full-time employees with appropriate skills, (iii) adequate annual operating expenditure, and (iv) physical office premises. An annual economic substance declaration with supporting evidence must be filed with SIFA; a customs brokerage IC lacking on-island staff, premises, and management will be treated as a substance-less shell and exposed to penalty, information exchange, and strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of Samoa-source income from any domestic return; falsely declaring in the AR-IC that no domestic business is conducted while deriving fees from Samoan-resident importers; using an exempt IC to circumvent the 27% domestic CIT on customs brokerage fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2017: penalty tax of up to 150% of the tax shortfall, statutory interest accrual, criminal fines upon conviction, and confiscation of the benefit derived. False customs declarations separately trigger Customs Act penalties, suspension of the customs brokerage license, and permanent debarment from the broker interface.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face piercing of the corporate veil for deliberate evasion: civil restitution orders against personal assets, travel bans pending tax investigation, and imprisonment of up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a passive substance-less IC in the distribution and service centre category: no employees in Samoa, no physical premises, no board meetings or banking activity in Samoa, and no annual economic substance declaration submitted to SIFA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SIFA administrative penalties under the International Companies Act 1987: fines per violation, power to compel dissolution, compulsory exchange of information with foreign tax authorities, and removal from the International Companies Register (strike-off).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: After strike-off, directors remain personally liable for company debts incurred during the non-compliant period; foreign tax jurisdictions may re-characterize profits and issue personal tax assessments; travel bans may be imposed under mutual assistance requests.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Breach (Broker Payment Rails and Trade-Based Money Laundering)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain customer due diligence on offshore cargo owners; omission of suspicious transaction reports on Automated Broker Interface ACH settlements; facilitating third-party freight payments known to be connected to sanctions evasion, trade-based money laundering, or fraudulent invoicing of bonded transit shipments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act and SIFA AML directives: fines per contravention up to WST 100,000, revocation of AML compliance approval, freezing orders on bank accounts, and debarment from the Automated Broker Interface and wire payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal liability: imprisonment of up to 14 years for willful money laundering facilitation, personal fines, disqualification from acting as a director, and asset forfeiture orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Prohibited Domestic Trading by an International Company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Samoa IC performing licensed customs clearance for Samoan-resident importers, maintaining a physical business establishment in Samoa, or carrying on a domestic bonded warehouse operation beyond purely offshore administrative functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Loss of the IC tax exemption with retrospective re-assessment at the 27% CIT rate plus penalties; fines under the International Companies Act; mandatory conversion to a domestic company or de-registration; revocation of any customs brokerage license by the Samoa Revenue and Customs authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorized the prohibited domestic trade are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, customs duties, and penalties; wage arrestment, asset seizure, and travel restriction orders may be imposed during recovery proceedings.
